findings.evidence: `Pairing.lean:175` defines `IsRecutOfRightEqRight.recut_branch` with the same two branch equalities; lines 626–638 derive the new disjunction solely from that theorem and the two `left_ne_right` facts, while `Overlap.lean:460` only specializes the resulting wrapper.
findings.fix: Delete both exact-one wrappers and have consumers case-split on `(D.isRecutOfRightEqRight_recut ...).recut_branch`, deriving the needed inequality in each branch from the corresponding rectangle’s `left_ne_right`.
findings.issue: `recut_first_or_second_right_eq_second_right` repackages `IsRecutOfRightEqRight.recut_branch`, discarding its interval and middle-state data and adding inequalities obtainable from `first.left_ne_right`/`second.left_ne_right`; the typed theorem at `Commutation/Overlap.lean:424` merely forwards this duplicate API.

summary: The two exact-one-side declarations duplicate the stronger existing branch API instead of reusing it at their eventual consumers.
